subject: Decision: Skyline Therapeutics - Dedicated GPU SKU fit and memory contingency

Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance request — long-context RAG + high-volume embeddings

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. As we discussed, Skyline is preparing a dedicated capacity request tied to a pilot that mixes two distinct workloads:

- Retrieval-augmented generation with working contexts routinely in the 250k–600k token range (multi-doc RAG for therapeutic dossiers).
- High-throughput batch embeddings for nightly indexing and similarity search (several million short requests / day).

Two asks:
1) Which GPU SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) would you recommend for a Dedicated pool that balances memory headroom for the long-context RAG and cost-efficiency for embeddings?
2) What fallback strategies do you suggest if the model spikes OOM or latency breaches during peak inference?

I've attached a small workload extract (skyline_workload_profile.csv) and a sample request distribution. Procurement will want a hit on estimated monthly cost as well.

Can your team sketch a proposal by EOD Wednesday PST?

Best,
Marta
Marta Klein
Director, ML Platform
Skyline Therapeutics

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Marta Klein <marta.klein@skyline-tx.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-23T08:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance request — long-context RAG + high-volume embeddings

Hi all — dug into the attached profile and ran a few microbenchmarks using representative models (8k / 64k / 256k context variants) and embedding pipelines. TL;DR recommendation below, followed by rationale and fallbacks.

Recommendation (initial Dedicated pool):
- L4 nodes (inference-optimized) — 60% of baseline pool capacity
  - Primary purpose: high-throughput embedding workloads and low-cost short-context generation. L4 gives best tokens/$ for shallow workloads and handles millions of small embedding requests with low marginal cost.
- A100 80GB nodes — 30% of baseline pool capacity
  - Primary purpose: memory-bound RAG for the 250k–600k contexts with lower OOM risk than a quantized L4-only approach. A100 80GB provides balanced FP16/INT8 perf and large flat memory per device for mid-length KV caches.
- H100 80GB or H100 NVL (if available) — 10% of baseline pool capacity (hot-standby / low-latency tier)
  - Primary: short bursts where model variants require faster FP16 kernels or lower tail latency (inference-critical ranking/ensembling). Use for canary rollouts and highest-SLA traffic.

Why this mix:
- Cost vs memory: L4 is the most cost-efficient for embeddings and short contexts; however, for very long context RAG the KV cache size and activation memory push L4 to quantization and tiling strategies that reduce throughput and increase latency. A100 gives a strong middle ground with larger device DRAM and mature kernel performance for long attention runs. H100 is overkill cost-wise for steady-state long-context RAG but valuable for bursty, latency-sensitive operations.

Sizing notes (example baseline with 100 concurrent slots):
- 60 L4-equivalent slots (embedding-heavy throughput)
- 30 A100-equivalent slots (long-context RAG)
- 10 H100-equivalent slots (latency-critical)

Fallback & resilience strategy:
1) Automatic model variant routing: prefer A100 for requests with predicted context > 100k tokens; route short-context < 8k to L4. Use prompt prefix analysis in the router.
2) KV-prefix caching: persist common document prefixes to reduce token generation time and avoid repeating attention compute. Cache hot doc embeddings on A100 nodes so subsequent RAG calls shorten context.
3) Tiling + checkpointing: for contexts > 400k tokens, tile the context and run staged attention passes with deterministic stitching. This reduces peak memory footprint at the cost of extra I/O — we recommend using this only with A100/H100.
4) Graceful degradation policy: when memory pressure is high, automatically degrade to a lower context-aware model (e.g., chunked RAG with summary layer) with a fallback banner returned to the caller.
5) Autoscale policy & preemptive burst: maintain a configurable burst pool (10% of committed capacity) that can ephemeralize additional H100/A100 GPUs for known campaign windows.

Cost considerations:
- L4 tokens/$ >> A100 tokens/$ > H100 tokens/$ for most workloads. We’ll size committed reserve for A100 (predictable RAG throughput) and leave L4 to be a larger portion of steady committed pool because it pays off for embedding bulk.
- If Skyline wants to cap monthly spend, we can implement per-route cost ceilings and automatic routing to cheaper quantized variants when budget thresholds hit.

Operational notes / attachments:
- Attached cost workbook with a baseline monthly run-rate estimate (dedicated_sku_cost_estimate_q2.xlsx).
- Tiling and cache strategy summary (tiling_and_cache_strategy.pdf).

Open questions for Skyline to finalize sizing:
- Confirm peak hourly QPS / concurrency windows (needed to pick the committed slot count).
- Confirm acceptable latency SLOs for RAG and embeddings.
- Any regulatory constraints that require dedicated A100/H100 due to isolation? (we can mark certain pools as isolated).

If you want, we can spin up a short pilot: 10 A100 slots + 30 L4 slots for 2 weeks and run your sample traffic. That will give actual P50/P95 latency and memory headroom numbers.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance request — long-context RAG + high-volume embeddings

Marta — thanks Dev and Karthik. From a commercial perspective we can propose a 6-month Dedicated pilot with the mix Dev suggested: 60% L4 / 30% A100 / 10% H100.

Operational commits we can offer for the pilot:
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on the Dedicated pool; P95 latency targets to be defined after pilot benchmarking.
- Billing: monthly commit with a 20% blended discount on host rates for the first 3 months of the pilot.
- Trial terms: we’ll include one no-cost burst week (up to 10% extra capacity) to account for onboarding stress-testing.

Next steps: Karthik, please confirm a target baseline concurrency (e.g., 100 slots or 200 slots) for the proposal. Marta: if you can confirm peak QPS histogram and legal/finance contacts (procurement@skyline-tx.com is cc’d), we’ll finalize the quote and a pilot SOW.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We’re happy to run the pilot. For the initial baseline let’s assume 150 concurrent slots (we can scale after pilot).

Proposed time to kick off pilot onboarding call: Tuesday 2027-05-28 at 10:00 AM PT. Procurement (procurement@skyline-tx.com) will review the SOW and follow up on commercial items.

One clarification request before the kickoff: for the tiling approach you mentioned, what is the expected throughput penalty (rough percent) for contexts that must be tiled vs. native full-attention runs? If you can add a short note in the kickoff deck, that would help set expectations.

Best,
Alex
VP, Engineering Ops
Skyline Therapeutics
